### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **25** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**14** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via error.message (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line; a string literal in sys_user))_
- `content/docs/api/error-handling-client.mdx`  _(via error.message (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line; a string literal in sys_user))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (symbol, 56 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d576509c80575197b3218aeb1f55884e5ed06ea6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4e2ea755b58fda41b8bc883d5cf5dfeae839a702` — the merge of head `dc341a62b6e4f53ba6c03eeab721267d0fd13846` into base `d576509c80575197b3218aeb1f55884e5ed06ea6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4e2ea755b58fda41b8bc883d5cf5dfeae839a702 && git checkout 4e2ea755b58fda41b8bc883d5cf5dfeae839a702
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d576509c80575197b3218aeb1f55884e5ed06ea6 dc341a62b6e4f53ba6c03eeab721267d0fd13846 && git checkout -B drift-repro d576509c80575197b3218aeb1f55884e5ed06ea6 && git merge --no-ff dc341a62b6e4f53ba6c03eeab721267d0fd13846

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d576509c80575197b3218aeb1f55884e5ed06ea6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d576509c80575197b3218aeb1f55884e5ed06ea6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1 review (L1-d) · 2026-11-17T16:14Z

L1: ACCEPT
Head-sha: `6a8399c10ca7dde65ac4bb9d9135df9dc67f6594`

Read against claim 6951731843 and report 6953684073 on #34652. Merge base `73609d0d`, 4 commits, 26 files, +825/-51.

- **Not governed.** `check-governed-merges --pr 34915` reports 0 paths and 876 lines.
- **This touches a contract face.** It widens the spec translation schema (`Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`), so the seat's L2 on the schema face is owed before landing, as the claim says.

### Checklist
- **Closing keyword.** `Fixes #34652` is right. Every "Done when" item is met:
  - the extractor emits one key per labelled column;
  - the bundles carry the keys, and the console draws the translated header (pinned in zh-CN, ablation red);
  - the bundles are regenerated, with the 9 `import_sso_users` headers in all 10 shipped locales.
- **Scope.** Every path is inside the claim's file surface.
  - The three edited existing test files (`i18n-walk.test.ts`, `validate-translation-references.test.ts`, `useObjectLabel-actionResultDialog.test.tsx`) are the "(+ tests)" / "(+ test)" of the units the claim names.
  - `authorable-surface/system.json` is named under the regenerated spec artifacts.
  - The `validate-translation-references.test.ts` edits widen fixtures and add coverage-pin rows. No assertion was removed.
  - `ActionResultDialog.tsx` is untouched, as the claim allowed: `TableBlock` already draws the overlaid `columns[].label`.
- **Changeset.** It names all four packages whose `src/**` moved (`spec` minor, `lint`, `platform-objects` and `@object-ui/i18n` patch). Its sentences match the diff, including `translation-target-unknown` at severity `error` (`validate-translation-references.ts:329`).
- **Design.** The sibling `columns` map keeps `fields.<path>` a string leaf, so every existing bundle parses and reads unchanged. A resolver test pins that a bundle with no column key answers exactly as before.
  - Both levels are keyed by literal path, and that holds at all four sites: the spec resolvers, the walk, the lint and the console overlay.
  - The overlay only reads declared fields and declared columns, so an undeclared key adds nothing. The lint refuses each undeclared case with its own message: an unknown column, a field that is not a table, an unknown field, and a block the action does not declare.
  - The preflight lookup refactor (`lookupActionPreflightFieldLabel` → `lookupActionPreflightText`) keeps the locale chain and the non-empty-string rule.
- **Tests.** Real commands with counts at the head: spec 848/27189, lint 216/9163, platform-objects 123/2046, ui i18n 102/1896. There is one ablation for each tested behaviour (resolver, walk, lint rule, console overlay), each red and each restored to the HEAD blob.
  - The live reading is in zh-CN against a real console, with an en control and the served `/meta` read.
  - One hop used a Playwright re-send to work around #34912, which is declared and filed.
- **Docs and `.describe()`.** Both schema `.describe()` texts are new and accurate. `translation.mdx` is regenerated, and `i18n-standard.mdx` and `ui/translations.mdx` gain the key rows.
  - The skills key table (`skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md`) is now incomplete. It is governed, declared as `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` and filed as #34917.
- **CI at this head.** Changeset, PR size, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, spec property liveness and doc links are green. Build, Lint, Type Check and Test Core were still in progress at review time. Landing waits for all of them.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
- **S1 (PR body, one sentence).** "Measured on the surface" says the translation schema has no rows in `packages/spec/authorable-surface/*`, so no shard moved. That is false at this head.
  - `packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json` gains `system/ActionResultDialogTranslation:columns`, and it is in the PR's own file list.
  - The preflight `columns` gets no row only because `ActionPreflightTranslationSchema` is module-local.
  - Please correct the sentence. The row supports `Metadata-protocol: added`, so nothing else changes.

### Notes
- N1: The en bundle now carries the nine headers as en strings. They match the authored labels, so en reads the same either way.
- N2: The nine-column dialog wraps its headers, and `idp_pending` is untranslated in zh-CN. Both are noted in the PR body and are outside this card.

Landing: not governed. After the seat's schema-face L2 and full green CI on the final head, area o3-G lands it. A later push owes a delta read.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6a8399c10ca7dde65ac4bb9d9135df9dc67f6594`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts, packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts + packages/lint/src/i18n-walk.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, ui/packages/i18n/src/useObjectLabel.ts

Inputs read: card #34652 (body, triage 6938958236, claim 6951731843, os-dev-report 6953684073), PR #34915 (body, 26-file list, net diff against `main` at merge-base 73609d0d), and the check-runs on this head, re-read at 2026-11-17T16:40Z: 65 success, 13 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending. The remainder of the diff (four test files, eleven generated bundles, the regenerated reference page, two prose docs pages, the changeset body) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set of `ActionResultDialogTranslationSchema`: gains optional `columns`, a record of field path to a record of column path to string. Right. The node is a `strictObject`, so before this head a `columns` key was refused as unknown; no bundle that parsed before can carry one, and every such bundle parses and resolves unchanged. `fields` stays `Record of string to string`.
- Accept-set of the module-local `ActionPreflightTranslationSchema`: the same optional `columns`. Right, for the same reason (strict node; the only key before was `fields`).
- New refusal in `validate-translation-references.ts` (`checkActionAnswerTableColumns`, `translation-target-unknown`, error): it reads only `rawAction.resultDialog.columns` and `rawAction.preflight.columns` and returns at once when neither is present. Right, and not a narrowing: both addresses were refused wholesale by the strict schema before this head, so the set of accepted bundles only grows. No existing key's judgment moves; `checkActionResultDialogFields` and `checkActionPreflightFields` are untouched.
- Public surface of `i18n-resolver.ts`: `ResultDialogLike` and `PreflightLike` rows gain an optional typed `columns`; no export added or removed. Right. A zod-inferred action never satisfied these `Like` shapes structurally (`label` is `I18nLabel`, the shape says `string`), so the added optional member takes nothing from a caller that compiled before. `Type Check · consumer gates` and `Type Check · workspace` are green.
- Extraction (`i18n-walk.ts`): one new expected key per labelled column, on both blocks. Right. The only producer of a table field on `main` is `sys_user.import_sso_users` (#34647, merged the same day), and its nine keys are filled in all eleven bundles in this diff.
- Authorable-surface: the shard `packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json` DID move, by one row, `system/ActionResultDialogTranslation:columns`. The PR body's sentence that no shard moved, repeated in the review brief, is contradicted by the tree. The move is the correct one for an added key (the preflight node is module-local and carries no row), and `Spec property liveness` plus the repo gates are green on it. See nit N2.
- Derived gate families: answered by the head's check-runs, all green (Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · repo and tooling gates, Lint · docs and code guards, Test Core 1 to 10, Test UI 1 to 16, Live E2E UI, Build Core, Build Docs, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards).

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening) — agrees with the diff: an optional key on two strict nodes, nothing removed, nothing re-typed.

`Metadata-protocol: added` is right: a bundle author can write a key that was refused before, and the authorable-surface shard records it as one added row. The kind takes at least `minor` on the package it moves, and the changeset carries `@objectstack/spec: minor`. `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/platform-objects` and `@object-ui/i18n` at `patch` are acceptable: none of them publishes a new authorable key, and the lint refusal covers only addresses that could not parse before. The changeset body carries both declaration lines and the `Skills-docs` line. `Check Changeset` is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` in the os-dev-report: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Design deviation from the card (sibling `columns` map instead of `fields.PATH.columns.COL`): accepted. The card offered the nested form only as an example and noted its cost, that a field node could no longer be a string leaf. The sibling map avoids exactly that cost and is the reason the widening is backward compatible.
- `Skills-docs` follow-up: owed and correctly not in this diff (`skills/**` is governed). The seat files it before landing. Its scope is wider than adding two keys: `skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md` line 167 says `defineTranslationBundle` refuses any other key under `preflight`, which becomes false once this lands, and line 230 lists the dead-key refusals without the column ones. The follow-up card should name both sentences.
- Out-of-scope findings in the report: the `organizationId` 400 is filed as #34912; the two noted items (narrow reveal dialog wrapping nine headers, `idp_pending` option untranslated in zh-CN) have no carrier. They are outside this card and do not bear on this verdict; the seat decides whether to file them.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join; every change is an in-memory overlay on already-loaded metadata.
- Governed paths: none in the file list; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

`packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts` — holds. One module-local `ActionAnswerColumnLabelsSchema` shared by both nodes, optional on each, both key levels literal. Read against its first consumer (`resolveActionResultDialog` and `resolveActionPreflight`) and against the first producer (the regenerated bundles, where `"host.notified"` and `"error.message"` are single keys under `columns.rows`): schema, resolver and data agree. A flat string where the per-field map belongs is refused, which is the right refusal. The jsdoc sentence that `columns` is a sibling of `fields` and that a bundle with no column key reads exactly as before is true of the code.

`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts` — holds. `overlayAnswerColumnLabels` indexes `columns[field.path][column.path]` directly, never splitting on a dot; each column walks the locale chain on its own through the existing `lookupActionResultDialogText` and the renamed `lookupActionPreflightText` (same loop, same non-empty-string test as before); a column with no bundle string keeps its authored label, an inline locale map included; a field with no `columns` is the same reference, as the jsdoc says. The field-label path is behaviourally unchanged. `translateAction` carries both blocks through. Tried to break it with: a bundle with no `columns`, a `columns` entry for a non-table field (ignored, since only declared columns are mapped), a partially translated table (per-column fallback), and double overlay (server, then console: idempotent). All hold.

Implementing files, sentence by sentence against the contract:

- `packages/lint/src/i18n-walk.ts` — agrees. `pushAnswerTableColumns` emits `[block, 'columns', field.path, column.path]`, the address the schema declares and the resolvers read, for both blocks; an unlabelled column gets no key, as an unlabelled field row gets none.
- `packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.ts` — agrees. The declared set is built by the same test the resolver uses (`Array.isArray(field.columns)`), so the lint refuses exactly what the resolver never reads: a field path no table declares, a column path the table does not list, a block the action lacks. A key for a declared but unlabelled column is accepted, matching the resolver, which overlays it.
- `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts` — agrees with the rule as coded.
- `ui/packages/i18n/src/useObjectLabel.ts` — agrees. `actionResultDialog` and `actionPreflight` read the `columns` node whole with `returnObjects` and overlay declared columns only, with the same non-empty-string test as the spec resolver. The console question in the brief: yes. Both call sites (`useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx` lines 251 and 383, `RecordDetailView.tsx` lines 1587 and 1706) pass the block through these two functions before the dialog, and `ActionResultDialog.tsx` `TableBlock` (line 285) draws `resolveInlineI18nLabel(column.label, language) || column.path` from those rows. That file is outside the diff and was read, not reviewed. `Live E2E UI` and Test UI are green.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract on any shipped data; none is to be fixed on this head, since a code fix would move it):

- N1 (nit) — `i18n-resolver.ts`: `n.columns?.[field.path]?.[columnPath]` reads through the prototype. For a table field whose literal path is `constructor` (or `toString`, `valueOf`) with a column whose path is `name`, the lookup returns the string `Object` (or the method name) as a translated header. No shipped or plausible action has such a field path, and the console overlay is not affected (it rejects a non-object node). An own-property test would close it; follow-up material at most.
- N2 (nit) — PR body, "Measured on the surface": it says the translation schema has no rows in the authorable-surface shards and that no shard moved. The diff adds one row to `system.json`. The declaration line and the level are right regardless; the sentence should be corrected in the PR body, which does not move the head.
- N3 (nit) — `validate-translation-references.ts`: the unchanged comment on `RESULT_DIALOG_LEAVES` says "every key the schema declares beside `fields`"; `columns` is now a second keyed child. Comment only.
- N4 (nit) — `translation.zod.ts` and `i18n-resolver.ts`: the `objects…_actions` and `globalActions` convention lists name `preflight.columns` explicitly but leave `resultDialog.columns` under `resultDialog.*`. Consistent with how `resultDialog.fields` was already listed; noted only.
